The small coastal town of Gull Harbor sat at the edge of a gray, restless sea. Marcus had not been home in eleven years.

He stood on the pier as the fog rolled in, mirroring the uncertainty inside him. His chest tightened. His heart pounded against his ribs, and a chill ran down his spine. The air smelled of salt, diesel and something like regret.

His father's boat, the Margaret Ann, was still tied at the end of the dock. Its paint was peeling, and the name was faded by years of sun.

Marcus climbed aboard and ran his hand along the wheel. He realized that home was never a place. It was the people who waited for you. For the first time in years, he finally felt at peace, and he made peace with the boy he had been.
